key_concepts: Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy stored in sugar.
Photosynthesis requires carbon dioxide, water, and sunlight as raw materials.
Plants absorb water and minerals through roots, and xylem transports them to leaves.
Phloem transports sugars produced by photosynthesis from leaves to other plant parts.
Carbon dioxide enters leaves through stomata controlled by guard cells.
Chloroplasts in palisade mesophyll cells contain chlorophyll, which captures light energy.

The Calvin cycle uses ATP and NADPH to convert carbon dioxide into glucose.
Starch in leaves indicates photosynthetic food production and can be tested with iodine.

Photosynthesis and respiration are linked through carbon dioxide and oxygen cycles.
